messages:
kai: Quick sketch - proposing a latch + lateral-failover pattern for canary/A-B rollouts. The latch is a tiny, per-cohort decision cache that prevents flip-flopping and lets nearby nodes short-circuit full adjudication when a variant evicts. Thinking TTL ~30s and a generation counter. Thoughts on tradeoffs and where the adjudicator should live?

morgan: Can you say more about "lateral failover"? is that just proxying to a neighbor variant or a coordinated takeover?

kai: Lateral = neighbor nodes can temporarily serve traffic for the cohort if the primary variant reports degraded health. They consult the latch + decision cache first. If cache says "A stable, gen 5" they can take a 1-2s traffic slice without calling central judge. If cache expired -> fall back to full adjudication.

sylvia: I like decision cache but worry about staleness causing incorrect acceptance of a degraded model. TTL is important - 30s might be ok for latency-sensitive customers but too long for high-error spikes. Maybe use an adaptive TTL: short on error spikes, longer when stable.

kai: Agreed on adaptive TTL. Also propose a small additional field in latch: "observed_health_epoch" - incremented when probes cross thresholds so lateral actors know if latch is stale vs actively marked-bad.

anita: How does this interact with rollback/canary drain? If we let neighbors serve during transient errors, ops may think the canary passed. We need clear telemetry and a flag that marks any lateral takeovers in the rollout console.

oliver: Tradeoff: sidecar adjudicator vs central adjudicator. Sidecar pros: ultra-low latency decision path (local latch + probe), cheaper to scale per node, better isolation per tenant. Cons: logic duplication, harder to coordinate global constraints (burst budgets, cross-tenant limits). Central pros: single truth + easier ops, cons: extra RPC hop and single point to pressure.

kai: Thinking interface boundaries: keep a small, stable adjudicator API: decide(cohort, token) -> {variant, generation, source:[latch|central], reason}. Local sidecar implements a thin cache layer and forwards to central if unknown or contested. That keeps central for policy and sidecar for speed.

morgan: Implementation Q: where does the latch live? in the sidecar memory, a small ringdb on-node, or a networked cache (redis-ish)?

sylvia: Prefer in-sidecar memory + optional spill to a local on-disk cache for restart resilience. Network caches add cross-node coupling which defeats lateral independence. Use replication for multi-az behavior if we need cross-machine failover.

kai: POC config snippet I mocked up:
```yaml
adjudicator:
  mode: sidecar
  latch_ttl: 30s   # adaptive algorithm can override
  latch_hysteresis: 3  # require 3 consecutive probes to flip
  decision_cache:
    max_entries: 5000
    eviction: lru
```

anita: We also need to store a brief event log for each cohort decision (timestamp, gen, reason) so postmortems can show lateral takeovers. Small append-only buffer in sidecar.

oliver: Good call. Also think about a "safety circuit": if lateral takeovers exceed threshold, auto-block new canaries for that tenant until human review. That logic should live centrally but be triggered by sidecar events.

kai: Agreed. I'll add the safety circuit as a central policy that subscribes to sidecar event streams. Sidecar emits simple events (json lines), central aggregator computes windows.

anita: Telemetry hooks: tag events with rollout_id, cohort_id, variant, gen, observed_health_epoch, and "source" (latch|probe|central). Make these queryable in the console.

morgan: Any perf/scale concerns? storing thousands of latches per node could blow memory for noisy tenants.

sylvia: cap by cohort cardinality + GC. Cap per-tenant latches and move cold cohorts to central cache. Also offload heavy cohorts to Dedicated pools so sidecars are lighter.

kai: Action items: 1) I will add RFC section for latch schema + adaptive TTL alg. 2) anita + oliver to draft event schema and safety-circuit thresholds. 3) sylvia to prototype sidecar in Rust with in-memory latch + disk spill.

devops-bot: Deploy: canary/adjudicator-poc job queued by morgan - expected runtime ~ 45m :hourglass_flowing_sand:

anita: Thanks - if we can include a small UI flag for "lateral takeover seen" in the rollout dashboard, ops will breathe easier.

kai: Yep - console hook in the RFC. Will drop a link to the draft in #docs when ready. Thanks all :thumbsup:
